name: stacklist
description: Save links and notes as cards, organize them into stacks, and search and read your Stacklist library, from ChatGPT.

interface.longDescription:
Stacklist is where you save links and notes as cards and group them into stacks. This app connects your Stacklist account to ChatGPT so you can work with your library in conversation.

Sign in with your Stacklist account. ChatGPT then sees only what your account can see: your own stacks and cards, plus stacks shared with you through a workspace or as a collaborator.

What you can do
- Browse your stacks and read the cards inside them, with titles, notes, links, tags and images.
- Search your cards and stacks by keyword, and open a card's summary or full text.
- Save links, notes and AI-written research as cards. Titles, descriptions and images are filled in from the page.
- Create stacks, rename them, edit their notes and reorder their cards.
- Remove cards and delete stacks you no longer need.
- Write long-form articles as private drafts.

How it handles your data
- New stacks are private unless you ask for public, and they do not appear on your profile until you feature them in Stacklist.
- Deleting has a confirmation step. Unless you have clearly named what to delete, ChatGPT shows what would be removed and waits for your yes. Deleting a stack keeps the cards inside it.
- ChatGPT cannot open other people's private stacks. A stack your account cannot access is reported as not found.
- Collections (groups of stacks) are not available through this app yet. ChatGPT will tell you so instead of changing something else.

Good to know
You need a Stacklist account to use this app. Profile editing, publishing and analytics stay in the Stacklist app. A good first step is asking ChatGPT what is in your stacks.
defaultPrompt: What stacks do I have on Stacklist, and what is in my most recently updated one?
Find the cards I saved about pricing pages and summarize what each one covers.
Create a private stack called Weekend reading for links I want to read later.

positive.prompt: What stacks do I have on Stacklist?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the demo account's stacks (Product design resources, Coffee shops in Brooklyn, Q4 planning) with privacy and last updated date. Read-only.

positive.prompt: Show me what is in my Coffee shops in Brooklyn stack.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the stack's cards in order, each with title, note and link. Read-only.

positive.prompt: Find the cards I saved about pricing pages and summarize what each one covers.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the pricing-page cards and summarizes each from its saved summary and tags. Read-only.

positive.prompt: Summarize my Q4 launch plan article.
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes the private draft article by its sections (Goals, Timeline, Risks). Nothing is changed.

positive.description: Create a stack and save a link
positive.prompt: Create a private stack called Weekend reading and save https://www.paulgraham.com/greatwork.html to it.
positive.expected_behavior: After confirmation, creates a private stack named Weekend reading with one card titled from the page, and says the stack is private and not on the profile.

negative.description: Editing a collection, which this app cannot reach
negative.prompt: Add my Coffee shops in Brooklyn stack to my Weekend picks collection.

negative.description: Vague delete request without a clear target
negative.prompt: Clean up my account and delete the stacks I don't need anymore.
Show me the cards in the Acme hiring plan stack.

review.commerce_description: Stacklist does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: browse and search your stacks and cards, save links and notes as cards, create and organize stacks, and write articles as private drafts.
